newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria contracts new import inspection agent.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria contracts new import inspection agent.

text.p: Nigeria served notice on Tuesday that it was terminating the services of two import inspection agents and had appointed a new one effective May 1.

"The federal government has given notice of termination of contracts of Cotecna International Ltd (CIL) and Societe General de Surveillance (SGS) as pre-shipment inspection agents for imports in zones A and D respectively," said a central bank circular to port users.
It said Messrs Anglia International Service Ltd had been appointed as a pre-shipment agent for the country.
No reason was given for the changes.
Pre-shipment inspection was introduced in Nigeria in 1978 to check that the quality of imports conformed to what was declared on paper. SGS was the first agent to be contracted to do the job in 1979.
Following a rapid increase in volume of imports four others were appointed -- CIL, Bureau Veritas, Swede Control Intertek and ISC Services Ltd.
The central bank circular said the last three would continue to inspect imports and would be joined by Anglia International Service.
